notes.author: Primary care physician
notes.text:
Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 07/15/2026
Patient: Gaston Durgan, 87-year-old male

Mr. Durgan presents with complaints of back pain. Back pain began 07/07/2026 after lifting a laundry basket. He describes the pain as localized to the lower back without radiation or numbness. On examination, there is tenderness over the lumbar paraspinal muscles and limited range of motion due to discomfort. Neurological examination reveals normal strength and sensation in the lower extremities. Vital signs are within normal limits. The assessment is acute musculoskeletal back pain likely related to the recent lifting activity. The plan includes conservative management with rest, use of over-the-counter analgesics as needed, and avoidance of heavy lifting. The patient is advised to perform gentle stretching exercises and to follow up in two weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/02/2026
Patient: Gaston Durgan, 87-year-old male

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/02/2026: acute osteoporotic T11 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.
Interval increase in T11 vertebral body height loss compared with radiographs from 07/09/2026.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at T11 with associated bone marrow edema, indicating recent injury. The fracture shows interval progression in vertebral body height loss compared to prior imaging from 07/09/2026.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Consider management options for osteoporotic fracture as appropriate.

notes.title: Spine Intervention Consultation
notes.author: Interventional radiologist
notes.text:
Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/07/2026
Patient: Gaston Durgan, 87-year-old male

History:
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. On re-interview, the back pain began about six months ago, long before the 07/07/2026 episode of lifting a laundry basket; the earlier history was inaccurate. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis. Pain NRS 8/10 despite 8 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification.

Functional Assessment:
Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire score 19/24.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current pain management and brace use. Consider interventional options if pain persists or worsens.
